name: Plesetsk Site 43
best_known_for: World's most northerly orbital launch site — Russia's polar / Molniya military + GLONASS pad
credit: Soyuz pad at Plesetsk Cosmodrome, 62.9°N — the highest-latitude orbital launch site that has ever flown. Originally an R-7 / R-9 ICBM base from the late 1950s; converted to space launches in 1966. Site 43 specifically operates Soyuz-2 today and historically hosted more orbital launches than any single site in the world for several decades. Russia's polar / Molniya / GLONASS workhorse, plus military payloads. The high latitude limits useful inclinations but suits sun-synchronous, Molniya, and high-inclination orbits. Coordinates from Russian Ministry of Defence + Roscosmos public records.
